title: Risk Factors for Increased Blood Loss and Requirement of Blood Products and Vasopressor Support during Craniosynostosis Surgery in Children
summary:
Background: In some infants, one or more of the growth seams of the skull close too early, so the head cannot grow normally. Treating this usually requires an operation during the first year of life. Such surgery can involve considerable blood loss, so the children often need blood transfusions and medication to support their circulation.
Research question: We want to find out which characteristics of a child and of the operation are linked to losing more blood during the procedure and to a greater need for blood transfusions and circulation-supporting medication.
Methodology: To do this, we retrospectively review the existing medical records of all children who were operated on for this condition at the hospital in Munich between the years 2014 and 2024. Only data that arose as part of the usual treatment are used; the children are not examined additionally for this purpose. The analysis is carried out in a way that does not allow any conclusions about individual children. The aim is to identify children at risk earlier in the future and to make treatment safer.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all children aged 0–1 year who underwent surgical treatment of craniosynostosis at Klinikum Großhadern between 2014 and 2024. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Surgical treatment of craniosynostosis at Klinikum Großhadern (LMU Munich) between 01/01/2014 and 31/12/2024. Both sexes as well as syndromic and non-syndromic forms are included.
Exclusion criteria:
No explicit exclusion criteria were defined.
